cropDiagnoses.primaryIssue: Fall Armyworm Whorl Infestation (सैनिक कीट / फॉल आर्मीवर्म)
cropDiagnoses.visibleEvidence: Parallel-veined monocot foliage forming a central whorl typical of young maize. Severe whorl damage featuring chewed/ragged leaves, heavy accumulation of brownish frass (sawdust-like insect excrement), and a visible caterpillar feeding deep inside the plant whorl.
actionableSteps: Handpick and destroy visible caterpillars from the plant whorls in early morning or late evening.
Apply dry sand mixed with neem cake powder or wood ash directly into the central plant whorls to disrupt feeding and smother larvae.
Apply neem-based formulations (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm) directly targeted into the central whorl of affected and surrounding plants.
preventativeMeasures: Install Fall Armyworm pheromone traps (4–5 traps per acre) for early monitoring of adult moth activity.
Practice intercropping maize with legumes (e.g., cowpea) or border cropping with Napier grass to reduce moth egg laying.
Conserve natural predators such as parasitoid wasps, earwigs, and ladybird beetles by avoiding unguided broad-spectrum chemical sprays.
cropDiagnoses.disclaimer: AI preliminary diagnostic observation. Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agricultural extension officer before chemical intervention.
cropDiagnoses.escalationNotes: Fall Armyworm can cause critical yield loss rapidly during early growth stages. Immediate field-wide scouting and targeted whorl treatment are recommended.
followUpQuestions: How widespread is this whorl damage and frass accumulation across your maize field?
How many days old is your maize crop or what growth stage (number of open leaves) has it reached?

cropDiagnoses.visibleEvidence: Broad parallel-veined leaves characteristic of a monocot. The central whorl shows heavy shredding, ragged chewing damage, and distinct granular sawdust-like frass accumulated within the leaf funnel. A caterpillar larva is visibly nestled inside the damaged whorl tissue.
actionableSteps: Manually handpick and destroy the visible larvae found inside the whorls if the affected field area is small.
Release egg parasitoids such as Trichogramma spp. as an early biological control measure.
Apply fine sand, wood ash, or soil mixed with lime directly into the whorl to irritate and desiccate early-instar larvae.
preventativeMeasures: Install pheromone traps (5 per acre) for mass trapping and monitoring of adult male moths.
Practice deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to predatory birds and solar heat.
Intercrop maize with legumes like cowpea or pigeon pea to attract natural predators and confuse pest host-seeking behavior.
cropDiagnoses.disclaimer: This assessment by KrishakDrishti AI is a preliminary optical advisory based solely on visual symptoms. It does not replace certified professional agricultural extension advice. For severe infestations or chemical pesticide recommendations, consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or state agricultural university guidelines.
cropDiagnoses.escalationNotes: The infestation level in the central whorl is severe and threatens the growing point of the young maize plant. If left unchecked, it can lead to complete defoliation or dead heart. Consult local agricultural authorities for safe, recommended bio-pesticides or selective insecticides if cultural methods fail.
